key_insight: The paper reframes visual generation from pixel-level appearance synthesis to 'intelligent' generation grounded in structure, dynamics, domain knowledge, and causality, proposing a five-level taxonomy that culminates in agentic world modeling.
problem_solved: Addresses current models' failures in spatial reasoning, persistent state, long-horizon consistency, and causal understanding by defining a roadmap and evaluation criteria to build visually plausible, stateful, and causally coherent generation systems.
method: Introduce a five-level taxonomy that traces evolution from atomic mapping (appearance-only) to agentic world models (structured, dynamic, goal-directed visual systems).
Characterize capabilities and failure modes at each level and propose evaluation dimensions/benchmarks to measure spatial, temporal, and causal competence.
Outline architectural/functional components for agentic visual models (perception, memory/state, dynamics, planning and domain knowledge integration) as a design blueprint.
impact: Provides practitioners a clear roadmap and evaluation framework to push generative models toward stateful, reasoning-capable visual systems—enabling reliable editing, simulation, and embodied-agent applications beyond photorealism.
visual_elements: Five-level taxonomy ladder/stack diagram (levels labeled from atomic mapping → structured → dynamic → knowledge-grounded → agentic world modeling).
Before/after example panels showing current appearance-only output vs. agentic, stateful scene edits across time steps.
Architectural pipeline illustrating perception → memory/state module → dynamics predictor → planner/agent loop.
Bar or radar chart comparing current model capabilities vs. target capabilities across spatial reasoning, persistence, long-horizon consistency, and causal understanding.
paper_title: Visual Generation in the New Era: An Evolution from Atomic Mapping to Agentic World Modeling
paper_authors: Keming Wu, Zuhao Yang, Kaichen Zhang, Shizun Wang, Haowei Zhu
